reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer pointed out that the current implementation may not work correctly for drivers that return page cache folios from ->fault(), and suggested using 'rmappable' instead of 'anon'. Additionally, they noted that DAX complicates this issue by setting folio->mapping but installing the folio itself.

Reviewer Lorenzo pointed out a potential simplification in the file_folio_not_uptodate function, suggesting replacing the folio_test_anon check with a VM_WARN_ON_ONCE assertion to ensure that the function is only called from where it can safely return true.

Reviewer Lorenzo suggested removing the unlikely() keyword from the file_folio_not_uptodate() check because it's already implied by the return case being VM_FAULT_NOPAGE, which is an error path.
reviews.raw_body:
I guess you mean drivers that return non-page cache folios from ->fault()?
Because the driver could return page cache folios there (e.g. shmem), in
which case folio->mapping would be set (set on being added to the page
cache).

But also things are complicated by DAX (of course) which _does_ set
folio->mapping but installs the folio itself so won't reach the test
anyway.

So I think 'rmappable' is the better thing to say given DAX and, given this
is fiddly, maybe worth explicitly pointing out that ->fault might return
non-rmappable folios, e.g.:

	/*
	 * Drivers which specify ->fault() might return non-rmappable folios
	 * (in which case no PG_uptodate).
	 */

---

Technically folio_test_anon() can never return true based on where this is
called from right? Could this just be a:

	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(folio_test_anon(folio));
	/* ... comment */
	return folio->mapping;

Instead?

(Note that __folio_add_file_rmap() asserts on folio_test_anon(folio)).

---

As Pedro said, I think this unlikely() is probably unnecessary given the true
return case is implicitly unlikely.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
The author addressed a concern about the historical context of the issue, explaining that the problem dates back to 2007 when __do_fault() started dropping the folio lock around ->page_mkwrite(), and acknowledged that this predates any possible stable tree.

The author acknowledged that driver pages from ->fault() do not get PG_uptodate and agreed to add a comment to clarify this in the patch.

Author acknowledged that all callers pass a file folio and agreed to add an assert at the top of the helper to check for this condition, indicating a fix is planned.

Author responded to feedback about the placement of a retry check, initially preferring it at the call site but open to alternative suggestions.
reviews.raw_body:
The window is from 2007, when __do_fault() started to drop the folio
lock around ->page_mkwrite():

Fixes: 6967614761fd ("ocfs2: release page lock before calling ->page_mkwrite")

Not sure how useful such Fixes is. It predates any possible stable tree.

---

Yes. How about:

        /*
         * ->fault() can also return driver memory that is not in the page
         * cache. It never gets PG_uptodate.
         */

I would rather avoid "rmappable". These folios do get
folio_add_file_rmap_ptes() in set_pte_range(), and the word reads like
PG_large_rmappable. As you said, DAX never reaches the check, so "page
cache" is accurate.

---

Right, all callers pass a file folio.

I will make it an assert, but at the top of the helper, so it checks
every call and not only the rare !uptodate one.

---

As I told Pedro, I prefer it at the call site. That is where the reader
needs to see that the retry is the rare path. But if you insist...

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Reviewer Matthew Wilcox argued that the patch is working around a bug in filesystems that clear PG_uptodate after ->page_mkwrite(), and suggested that these filesystems should be fixed instead.
reviews.raw_body:
Filesystems that do this are buggy.  They shuld be fixed, not worked
around like this.

2026-11-09.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug where the Linux kernel fails to update the page cache after a write operation, leading to stale data being read from disk. The issue occurs when encryption fails and the folio is left in an inconsistent state. To fix this, the patch rechecks the PG_uptodate flag after the ->page_mkwrite() function returns with the folio locked. If the flag is clear, it retries the fault to read the folio in again from disk. This ensures that the page cache remains consistent and up-to-date.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that the patch should not map a folio that is not uptodate until filesystem fixes land, and suggests using WARN_ON_ONCE() and SIGBUS to flag buggy filesystems.
reviews.raw_body:
Fair. What is your take on the way out?

Is there a timeline for the filesystem fixes?

Until they land, mm should still not map a folio that is not uptodate.

Would WARN_ON_ONCE() and SIGBUS, like the other checks in 2/2, work for
you? It flags the buggy filesystem instead of hiding it.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch's retry mechanism for a folio marked as !uptodate after ->page_mkwrite() is unnecessary, as other VM assertions will eventually trip due to this condition.
reviews.raw_body:
It doesn't matter which way round the race ends up; if a filesystem marks
a mapped folio as !uptodate, there are other VM assertions that will
trip eventually.  This is one of those cases where we should ignore the
bot because it doesn't quite know enough.

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug where the Linux kernel fails to update the page cache after a write operation, leading to stale data being read from disk. The issue occurs when encryption fails and the folio is left in an inconsistent state. To fix this, the patch rechecks the PG_uptodate flag after the ->page_mkwrite() function returns with the folio locked. If the flag is clear, it retries the fault to read the folio in again from disk. This ensures that the page cache remains consistent and up-to-date.
